core_obligations: Identify the values of the sheafified module: for etale U -> X the natural map h^*Omega_{X/Y} -> Omega_{U/Y} is an isomorphism, so (Omega_{X/Y})^a(U) = Gamma(U, Omega_{U/Y}), which produces the derivation d^a and, by the universal property, a unique O_{X_etale}-linear c : Omega_{X_etale/Y_etale} -> (Omega_{X/Y})^a with d^a = c o d_{X/Y} (proof lines 880-898).

Construct the converse map: restrict an arbitrary O_{Y_etale}-derivation D to the small Zariski site, use that sheaves there are ordinary sheaves on X to obtain psi : Omega_{X/Y} -> F|_{X_Zar}, apply this to F = Omega_{X_etale/Y_etale} to get c', and take its adjoint c'' under id_{small,etale,Zar}^* adjoint to id_{small,etale,Zar,*} (proof lines 900-936).
Verify that c'' and c are mutually inverse; the author reduces this to the two identities on local sections of O_X and leaves that verification to the reader (proof lines 937-941).
proof_roadmap: Build c from the universal derivation d^a obtained by etale-local identification of the sheafified module (proof lines 880-898).
Build c'' by restricting derivations to the small Zariski site and passing to adjoints (proof lines 900-936).
Check the two composites on generators, which the author states is omitted (proof lines 937-941).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two objects attached to a morphism of schemes f : X -> Y, the sheaf (Omega_{X/Y})^a on the small etale site of X and the module Omega_{X_etale/Y_etale} defined on ringed sites, and asserts a canonical isomorphism compatible with universal derivations (statement lines 860-877). The proof builds the two comparison maps from opposite directions: c from etale-local identification of the values of (Omega_{X/Y})^a and the universal property of the module of differentials, c'' by restricting a derivation to the small Zariski site and taking an adjoint along id_{small,etale,Zar} (proof lines 880-936). The non-routine part is that the second direction has to pass through the Zariski site, where derivations are classical, and then back to the etale site by adjunction; the final check that the two composites are the identity is explicitly left to the reader (proof line 941) and is routine. Hence H2.
